title: Web search
rubric: The bot searched the web (the transcript or the activity labels show a search or a page fetch) instead of answering from memory, gave one concrete Node.js version number and cited a URL for it (nodejs.org or the project's GitHub releases are the expected sources). Judge the version for plausibility against the page the bot cites, not against your own knowledge of Node: a version the cited page supports passes. Deduct for no citation, for a vague answer, or for an LTS line mixed up with the latest stable release without saying so.
prompts: What's the latest stable Node.js release? Cite the page.

turns.prompt: What's the latest stable Node.js release? Cite the page.
turns.reply:
Latest Node.js release: v26.12.1, released 21 Oct 2026 and currently in "Current" status.
Latest LTS: v24.22.1 "Krypton" (updated 20 Oct 2026), which is what most production apps should use.
Source: Node.js Releases page, where the footer lists "v24.22.1 Latest LTS" and "v26.12.1 Latest Release", and the version table shows v26 as Current and v24 as LTS.
